learn.title: Wave Energy Converters
learn.intro: Wave energy captures the sun's heat-driven ocean motion to generate clean electricity. Unlike solar or wind, waves are predictable and dense, offering a reliable renewable source. With over 50% of the global population living near coasts, wave energy could power millions of homes while minimizing land use conflicts.
learn.c1_text: An oscillating water column (OWC) uses wave motion to push air through a turbine. As waves enter a chamber, they compress and decompress the trapped air, spinning a bidirectional turbine. Think of it like breathing: inhale pushes air out, exhale pulls it back in—both turning the same turbine.
learn.c2_text: Point absorbers float on the surface and convert wave motion into mechanical energy via internal hydraulic rams or gyroscopes. A buoy moves up and down on a fixed spar, driving a generator below the waterline. These systems can be deployed in arrays, much like offshore wind farms.
learn.c3_text: India has identified 300 GW of theoretical wave energy potential along its 7,500 km coastline. The Ministry of New and Renewable Energy supports pilot projects, including a 1 MW demonstration off Tamil Nadu. National Institute of Ocean Technology leads R&D for indigenous wave energy converters.
learn.stat3: India's identified wave energy potential: 300 GW
learn.stat4: World's first commercial wave farm: 3 MW in Australia

learn.title: Flow Batteries for Grid Storage
learn.intro: Flow batteries store renewable energy in liquid electrolytes held in external tanks. Unlike lithium-ion batteries that store energy in solid electrodes, flow batteries decouple power and energy, enabling scalable, long-duration storage. This makes them ideal for balancing grids powered by intermittent solar and wind.
learn.c1_text: Vanadium redox flow batteries (VRFBs) use vanadium ions dissolved in sulfuric acid. Energy is stored in the difference between V²+/V³+ and VO²+/VO²+ states. When discharging, electrons flow through an external circuit while ions pass through a proton exchange membrane, generating electricity without degradation.
learn.c2_text: Iron-chromium and zinc-bromine flow batteries offer lower-cost alternatives using abundant metals. Iron-based systems avoid vanadium’s price volatility and toxicity. They operate at ambient temperatures and can scale independently for power and energy, making them suitable for utility-scale applications requiring 4–12 hours of discharge.
learn.c3_text: India aims to deploy 4-hour battery storage with solar projects under the Production Linked Incentive scheme. Startups like Exicom and Tata Chemicals are developing flow battery pilots. The National Mission on Strategic Technologies promotes domestic manufacturing of non-lithium storage solutions.
learn.stat3: India's target: 500 GW renewable capacity by 2030
learn.stat4: Flow battery lifespan: 20+ years with minimal degradation

learn.title: Floating Offshore Wind Platforms
learn.intro: Floating offshore wind unlocks stronger, steadier winds in deep waters beyond traditional fixed-bottom turbines. By mounting turbines on buoyant platforms tethered to the seabed, countries can harness vast renewable resources without shallow-water limitations. This technology is key to expanding offshore wind globally.
learn.c1_text: Spar platforms resemble giant buoyant cylinders extending deep below the water surface. They use ballast at the bottom to stay upright and stable. Mooring lines connect the platform to anchors on the seabed. This design is widely used in Norway’s Hywind project and offers excellent stability in harsh seas.
learn.c2_text: Semi-submersible platforms use multiple floating hulls connected by a deck structure. They displace water to provide buoyancy and stability without deep draft. Easier to assemble in port and install, these platforms dominate current commercial deployments like Kincardine in Scotland and are favored for mass production.
learn.c3_text: India has 600 GW of offshore wind potential, mostly in waters deeper than 40 meters. The Ministry of New and Renewable Energy plans to auction 30 GW of offshore wind by 2030. Floating wind pilots are being explored off Tamil Nadu and Gujarat coasts with international partnerships.
learn.stat2: Hywind Scotland: 30 MW floating wind farm
learn.stat4: Water depth limit for fixed turbines: 60 meters

learn.title: Green Hydrogen Production
learn.intro: Green hydrogen is produced by splitting water using renewable electricity, creating a clean fuel with zero emissions. It can store excess solar and wind power and decarbonize hard-to-abate sectors like steelmaking, shipping, and ammonia production. Scaling green hydrogen is critical for achieving net-zero economies worldwide.
learn.c1_text: Alkaline electrolyzers use liquid potassium hydroxide and nickel electrodes to split water. Lower-cost and mature technology, they suit large-scale, steady-state operations. Less responsive to load changes, they’re preferred for industrial applications where consistent power supply exists, such as ammonia plants.
learn.c3_text: India launched the National Green Hydrogen Mission with $2.3 billion investment to produce 5 MMT of green hydrogen annually by 2030. Reliance Industries and NTPC plan gigawatt-scale electrolyzer projects. The mission targets cost reduction to $1.5/kg by 2030 through domestic manufacturing and scale.
learn.stat1: India's green hydrogen target: 5 MMT/year by 2030
learn.stat4: India's National Green Hydrogen Mission budget: $2.3 billion

learn.title: Virtual Power Plants
learn.intro: Virtual power plants (VPPs) aggregate thousands of distributed energy resources—rooftop solar, home batteries, EVs—into a single controllable entity. Using AI and real-time data, VPPs balance supply and demand across the grid, enhancing reliability while unlocking revenue for participants. They represent the future of intelligent, decentralized energy systems.
learn.c1_text: VPPs use software platforms to remotely monitor and dispatch distributed assets. Each device—from a Tesla Powerwall to an electric car—acts as a small power plant. When aggregated, these resources can rival the output of conventional power stations. AI algorithms predict demand and optimize dispatch timing for maximum efficiency.
learn.c2_text: VPPs integrate demand response by shifting consumption to times of high renewable generation. Smart thermostats adjust cooling loads, and industrial consumers reduce usage during peaks. This dynamic balancing prevents blackouts and reduces reliance on fossil peaker plants, creating a more flexible and resilient grid ecosystem.
learn.c3_text: India launched its first VPP pilot in 2022 aggregating rooftop solar and storage across 15,000 homes in Delhi and Haryana. Supported by the Ministry of Power and NITI Aayog, the initiative explores peer-to-peer energy trading and grid stabilization services. Tata Power and Siemens are leading technology deployment.
learn.stat1: Germany's largest VPP: 100+ MW aggregated capacity
learn.stat2: Tesla Virtual Power Plant: 150,000+ connected devices

learn.title: Capacity Factor Explained
learn.intro: Capacity factor measures how much electricity a power plant actually produces compared to its maximum possible output. It reveals the real-world performance gap between nameplate ratings and actual generation. Understanding capacity factor helps compare intermittent renewables like solar and wind with steady sources like coal or nuclear.
learn.c1_text: A 100 MW solar farm with a 25% capacity factor generates 219,000 MWh annually—equivalent to running at full power for just 876 hours per year. Wind farms average 35–50%, while coal plants reach 80–90%. The metric exposes intermittency challenges and informs energy planning decisions.
learn.c2_text: Solar capacity factors depend on sunlight hours, latitude, and weather. Desert installations exceed 30%, while northern regions drop below 15%. Wind varies by location—offshore sites often hit 50% due to consistent breezes. Maintenance downtime and curtailment during oversupply also reduce effective output.
learn.c3_text: India's solar parks average 22–26% capacity factor due to tropical sunlight and monsoon interruptions. Wind farms in Tamil Nadu reach 30–35%. The government uses capacity factor data to set tariff benchmarks and plan hybrid projects combining solar-wind-storage to improve overall utilization rates.
